request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Each line reads `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`, oldest first. The date is the sheet's today when the change was made. The due is the one shown on screen at that moment: the settled due once a claim is settled, otherwise its figure plus any late charge, and `n/a` if no rate applied.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V25__claim_log.sql`, adds a `claim_log` table. Claims that already existed start with an empty log, because their past statuses can't be rebuilt.
- **Writing the log:** a new `ClaimLogStore` writes a line in the same transaction as each change:
  - when a claim is added, from either the claim form or quick add (`SaveClaimAdded`);
  - on every single status change (`SaveClaim`), which covers open, settle, pending, approve, reject and void;
  - for each claim a bulk open actually opens (`OpenClaims`).

  A refused action is rolled back, so it writes no line.
- **Reading it:** each claim returned by the server now carries its log lines (`ClaimResponse.log`, filled in by `RespondWithClaims` and `RespondWithClaim`).
- **Front end:** every claim row lists its log, one `claim-log-line` element per line (`features/claims/list.slot.tsx`), and the `Claim` type has the new `log` field.

The request didn't ask for a new audit record, so I didn't add one.
